text:
maya: FYI tenant-42 (dedicated eu-west-1) reporting repeated 503s and 2-4s tail latency on /v1/generate. Customer sent request-id: 0x9f3b7 and a curl that reproduces. Need repro bundle + node + GPU metrics so SRE can correlate. @sre-oncall can you collect pod logs, dmesg, and nvidia-smi traces?

olivia: pls paste the curl and exact timestamps so we can match request logs. also confirm if this affects all models or just large-llama-13b-quant.

maya: here's the curl they sent (sanitized):
```
curl -v "https://dedicated-eu-west1.redwood/api/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "X-Request-ID: 0x9f3b7" \ 
  -d '{"model":"large-llama-13b-quant","prompt":"hello"}'
```
They reported first spike at 2025-11-02T13:12:21Z and subsequent errors at ~13:12:40Z, 13:13:05Z. Customer says only ~5% of requests fail but latency spiky for same window.

rafael: taking this. First steps: collect debug bundle and live GPU sampling. Run on the control-plane node that can reach tenant-42 namespace, or I'll run from bastion. Commands I want collected: 
```
# pod list
kubectl -n tenant-42 get pods -o wide

# recent logs for inference container (include previous)
kubectl -n tenant-42 logs <POD> -c inference --since=30m --tail=500

# node dmesg & journal (if possible)
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200
sudo journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager -n 500

# GPU telemetry (sample for 1-2 minutes)
watch -n 1 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1
```
I'll also want to correlate with our request logs in the control plane, so include the exact request-id header and timestamp (we have 0x9f3b7).

jin: if you can run redwoodctl (preferred) it will collect everything into a single bundle: 
```
redwoodctl debug-bundle collect --tenant tenant-42 --since 2025-11-02T13:10:00Z --until 2025-11-02T13:20:00Z --request-id 0x9f3b7 --output /tmp/tenant-42-0x9f3b7.tar.gz
```
Then upload to our support bucket: 
```
aws s3 cp /tmp/tenant-42-0x9f3b7.tar.gz s3://redwood-support/debug-bundles/tenant-42/1813456789-0x9f3b7.tar.gz --profile support-uploader
```
If you can't run redwoodctl, gather the files above and tar them with a small README that includes the request-id and timestamps.

maya: customer said they can't run privileged commands. They gave us a kube service account token we can use to `kubectl logs` into inference pods. Token TTL is short so we should act now. Token name: sa-tenant42-support-20251102 (redacted).

rafael: ok I'll use the token from the secure vault and pull logs. I'll also attach a short script to continuously sample nvidia-smi for 2 minutes and collect perf counters.

sre-oncall: pinged. I'll run the following on the node where the failing pod landed (I'll paste exact pod names in next message):
```
# sample script to run on the node (nohup to background)
for i in {1..120}; do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv >> /tmp/gpu-sample-$(date +%s).csv; sleep 1; done &
sudo dmesg --time-format iso > /tmp/dmesg-tail.txt
sudo journalctl -u docker --no-pager -n 200 > /tmp/docker-journal.txt || true
```
I'll attach these to the debug bundle.

deploy-bot: deploy finished for ded-cluster-2 @ 2025-11-02T12:58:10Z :rocket:

olivia: note from billing side: tenant-42 recently moved to dedicated reserved capacity, they reported a billing spike this morning that might be related to retry storms. keep finance in the loop if we see high token counts from replays.

rafael: found pods: inference-0, inference-1, controller-2 in tenant-42. Pulling logs for inference-0 now. If anyone on call wants repro, use the curl above + header X-Request-ID:0x9f3b7.

maya: thanks. Customer asked for ETA on when we'll have the bundle — can we get a preliminary dump in next 30m?

rafael: yes, I'll upload an initial bundle (logs + gpu samples) within 25m to s3 and ping here with link. If anyone sees obvious OOMs or GPU driver errors in the dmesg I'll flag immediately.

jin: one more ask — include the inference container's /var/log/inference/debug.log and the runtime metrics endpoint response: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/metrics` from inside the pod (if allowed). That helps with queue depth and batching artifacts.

sre-oncall: ack, collecting everything now. will post S3 link when complete. :thumbsup:
